question: A brief written before the score existed reaches dispatch — what model runs it?

options.label: No score means no model flag — `dispatch.host` runs as it does today
options.reason: Every board and every approved brief that exists keeps working untouched, and the migration adds a nullable field and backfills nothing. Turning the whole feature off stays a matter of not scoring, which is the conservative default `DEFAULT_CONFIG` already argues for.
options.costLater: Two invocation paths live side by side forever. “Why did this node run on the default model” has two answers — no score, or a score whose tier is empty — and every surface that reports the model has to say which.

options.label: The migration backfills every existing brief at the middle of the scale
options.reason: One path through `dispatch.ts`, and the model a node ran on is a fact somebody can read off the record for every node on the board rather than for the ones written after today.
options.costLater: A backfilled score is a number nobody chose, and a year later it reads exactly like one an agent judged — the failure ADR 0049 avoided by recording `did-not-run` instead of `passed`. The migration is also one-way: a v5 board coming back from a teammate carries it.

options.label: A brief without a score cannot be approved
options.reason: The score decides what a run costs, so it belongs to what the human approves beside the acceptance list — the same argument ADR 0027 makes about criteria being the definition of done.
options.costLater: Every already-approved brief on the board has to be rewritten before its node can run, and `approve` gains a refusal about a field the person approving did not write themselves.
